description: Replace the repair CUTSCENE with a Royal Match style in-place repair animation. Today a repair cuts to a black screen with the task title, a work VFX, a horizontal wipe and an italic story line, running 4.2 seconds. Royal Match never cuts away: the task popup closes, the room stays exactly where it is, gold sparkles trace the thing being repaired, the room art crossfades under them, and it is over in well under two seconds with no text on screen at all. Reference: docs/royal-match/03-repair-in-place.jpg, which is a repair caught mid-play — sparkle trails over the carpet, the live room behind them, the area button still on screen. The kit's own animation, particles and VFX must not regress (tools/check_vfx_intact.py). The arc-beat cutscenes in CutsceneRunner.cs are a SEPARATE feature and must not be touched.

userStories.title: A repair always plays on the room that is already on screen
userStories.description: As a player, I want a repair to happen on the room I am looking at, so that the game never cuts to a black screen for it.
acceptanceCriteria: StoryRepair.Perform resolves a room RectTransform from AreaScreen.Instance.RoomRect when the area page is open, and from the home screen's room when it is not
RepairCutscene.Play is called with that room rect, so the over-room path runs instead of the own-screen path
The black backdrop stays fully transparent whenever a room rect was supplied
The own-screen path is still reachable and unchanged when no room exists (kit scenes, map, tests)
Typecheck passes: python3 tools/make_typecheck_csproj.py && dotnet build Story.Typecheck.csproj -v q --nologo
python3 tools/check_vfx_intact.py reports no regressions

userStories.title: No text on screen while a repair plays
userStories.description: As a player, I want the repair to be something I watch, not something I read, so that it feels like Royal Match rather than a slideshow.
acceptanceCriteria: While playing over a room, RepairCutscene shows no task title, no story line and no 'tap to skip' hint
The own-screen fallback path keeps its title and line, so nothing is lost where there is no room to play on
Tapping still skips the repair to its end state
Typecheck passes
Unity screen tests pass: StoryScreenTests.RunHeadless prints 'Screen tests passed.'

userStories.title: Retime the repair to Royal Match's beat map
userStories.description: As a player, I want the repair over in about a second and a half, so that spending eight stars on an area is not eight cutscenes.
acceptanceCriteria: Over a room the beats are: sparkle in at 0.0, peak 0.45, reveal 0.60, settle 1.10, end 1.50 seconds
No camera push-in and no stage scaling when playing over a room — the room does not move
The 4.2 second beat map is kept for the own-screen fallback path
The beat times are named constants with a comment saying where they came from
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Find the repaired region by diffing the before and after room art
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to know WHERE in the room a repair happened, so that the sparkles can sit on the thing being repaired instead of washing the whole picture.
acceptanceCriteria: New static helper (e.g. StoryArt.ChangedRect(areaId, state)) returns a normalised Rect covering the pixels that differ between state-1 and state art
The result is cached per (areaId, state) — it must not resample a 1500px sprite every repair
Returns the room's centre third when the two sprites are the same object or either is null
Sprites are read without requiring Read/Write enabled, or the importer setting is applied by tools/ and documented
An editor test asserts the rect for one area with per-state art is smaller than the full room and inside 0..1
Typecheck passes
Unity screen tests pass

userStories.title: Gold sparkle burst localised on the repaired region
userStories.description: As a player, I want gold sparkles over the thing being fixed, so that I can see what my star bought.
acceptanceCriteria: RepairVfx gains a Royal sparkle effect: gold star particles rising and fading, plus one soft warm flash, tuned off docs/royal-match/03-repair-in-place.jpg
The emitter is positioned and sized from US-004's changed rect, not the whole room
It is the effect used for every work type when playing over a room; the eight per-work effects stay for the own-screen path
No kit ParticleSystem, prefab or sprite is modified — the effect is additive and built by Story code
Typecheck passes
python3 tools/check_vfx_intact.py reports no regressions
Verified in the running player: build with StoryBuild.BuildMac, launch at 402x874, screenshot the repair mid-play

userStories.title: The room crossfades to its repaired state instead of wiping across
userStories.description: As a player, I want the new room to appear under the sparkles, so that the change reads as the repair landing rather than a curtain being drawn.
acceptanceCriteria: Over a room, the after state fades in over the before state across the reveal beat rather than using Image.FillMethod.Horizontal
The neglect wash lifts over the same beat, so an area with a single restored picture still reads as a change
The horizontal wipe is kept for the own-screen fallback path
Typecheck passes
Verified in the running player

userStories.title: The task popup closes for the repair and comes back when it lands
userStories.description: As a player, I want the task list out of the way while the repair plays, so that I am watching the room and not a panel.
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing Do It hides the area panel before the first sparkle, not after it
The panel returns once the repair ends, showing the ticked-up progress bar
The area button and top bar stay visible throughout, as in the reference screenshot
No path can leave the panel hidden if the repair is skipped or errors
Typecheck passes
Unity screen tests pass
Verified in the running player

userStories.title: The spent star flies from the pressed row to the top bar
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see the star leave my pile, so that the cost of a repair is legible without reading a number.
acceptanceCriteria: On Do It, a star sprite tweens from the pressed row to the top bar's star pill and fades out there
The top bar's star count updates when the flying star arrives, not before
It uses StoryClock so the editor tests can drive it, per the Codebase Patterns section
Typecheck passes
Verified in the running player

userStories.title: Document the repair animation and delete what the cutscene left behind
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the Story layer's CLAUDE.md to describe the animation that now exists, so that the next change is made against the truth.
acceptanceCriteria: Assets/JellyGarden/Scripts/Story/CLAUDE.md describes the in-place repair, its beat map and the two paths (over-room and own-screen)
Any field, constant or helper in RepairCutscene left unused by US-001 to US-008 is removed, not left dead
The header comment at the top of RepairCutscene.cs matches what the file now does
Typecheck passes
Unity screen tests pass
python3 tools/check_vfx_intact.py reports no regressions
